steps.decision: Measurement system is marginal: percent GRR study variation (28.08%) sits in the AIAG marginal band (10-30%), percent tolerance (19.72%) is acceptable (<30%), but NDC=4.82 falls just short of the recommended floor of 5 distinct categories. Operator main effect (p=0.167) and part-by-operator interaction (p=0.377) are not significant, so almost all gage variation is repeatability rather than reproducibility. Readings can support a directional process conclusion but are marginal for discriminating closely similar parts.
Distribution is symmetric (skewness near 0) and Anderson-Darling p (approximate) = 0.477, consistent with normality.
Fail to reject normality (p=0.401 > 0.05, Shapiro-Wilk). process_run void-fraction readings can be treated as normally distributed for capability analysis.
No individuals or moving-range points exceed control limits (0 of 50 flagged). Process shows no special-cause signal across the run in build order; it is behaving as a stable, in-control process.

Cpk=1.42 and Ppk=1.34, both above the common 1.33 capability benchmark against the 0 to 25 percent-void-area spec. Both indices are numerically bound by the lower side (Cpl/Ppl) rather than the upper spec, an artifact of the mean sitting much closer in sigma units to the LSL=0 floor than to USL=25; it is not evidence of a real underfill risk since void fraction is physically bounded at zero.

route_decisions.chosen_branch: analyzed the repeat X-ray gage study before trusting process_run readings
used capability.normal (not nonnormal) because Shapiro-Wilk and Anderson-Darling both fail to reject normality
ran I-MR control chart on process_run before computing capability; 0 flags found, so proceeded with capability analysis on the full 50-point series

requested; steward reported outcome=refused, refusal=unroutable, and named only three topics available for this project (charter, repeat readings/MSA, void fraction/build order). No before/after or control-plan batch exists; report states this gap plainly rather than inventing an improvement narrative.
